docs.title: Design Standards
docs.text:
Contributor-facing conventions for the three first-class, convention-driven surfaces in obs:

  1. Local config file contracts — vault-rooted YAML maps that another command reads.
  2. Their related commands — the CLI verbs that create, validate, and consume a contract.
  3. Obsidian dashboards — deterministic, marker-bounded markdown rendered into a vault.

This is not a user tutorial. End users should read CLI Reference and The Research Board tutorial. The Architecture → Config File Contracts section is the code-level companion to §2 below.

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text:
A "design standard" here means: when you add a new local config contract, a config/sync command, or a vault dashboard, it must follow the patterns below. They exist so that every surface is validated, atomic, idempotent, and scriptable (non-interactive path + --dry-run where it writes). Deviations need an explicit ADR.

The canonical example of all three working together is .flow/obsidian-sync.yml:

  • the contract (§2) is a vault-rooted mirror map,
  • obs flow init creates it and obs doctor --layer flow validates it (§3),
  • and the research/action dashboards (§4) are the same shape of vault-writing surface.

docs.title: 2. Local Config File Contracts
docs.text: A config contract is a small YAML file obs reads to drive a sync or mirror operation. There is exactly one today: .flow/obsidian-sync.yml.

docs.title: Location & ownership
docs.text:
Property Value Path <vault_dir>/.flow/obsidian-sync.yml — vault-rooted, one per vault directory Owner obs flow init (v4.3.0) Validator obs doctor --layer flow (JSON Schema) Schema schema/obsidian-sync.schema.json

A config contract is vault-rooted, not project-rooted. Do not put repo/settings state in a vault file, and do not invent a second .obs/* or .flow/* map without extending this standard.

docs.title: Must
docs.text:
• Validate the file against a JSON Schema (schema/obsidian-sync.schema.json) before use.
  • Use a bare vault_root + pairs shape — no schema: / mirror: envelope.
  • Reject pair paths that start with / or contain .. (path-traversal guard).
  • Reject a vault/repo pair that is identical (no-op mirror).
  • Refuse to overwrite an existing file unless --force is passed.
  • Write atomically via os.replace(tmp, target) (never a bare open("w")).
  • On --force, back up the prior file to <file>.bak before replacing.

docs.title: Must not
docs.text:
• Emit a vault == repo identity pair.
  • Allow duplicate vault→repo mappings.
  • Read or write outside the vault tree (no .., no absolute paths in pairs).
  • Trust unvalidated YAML — a parse failure must surface as a clear error, not a crash.

docs.title: Worked example
docs.text:
A minimal valid .flow/obsidian-sync.yml:

vault_root: "~/Library/Mobile Documents/iCloud~md~obsidian/Documents/Research"
pairs:
  - { vault: "teaching", repo: "teaching" }
  - { vault: "04_gauge/teaching", repo: "01-gauge-pmed/teaching" }
include: ["*.md"]
exclude: ["_archive"]

Produced non-interactively by:

obs flow init ~/vaults/MyVault \
  --vault-root "~/Library/Mobile Documents/iCloud~md~obsidian/Documents/Research" \
  --pairs '[{"vault":"teaching","repo":"teaching"}]' --json

docs.title: 3. Related Commands
docs.text:
Every contract ships two commands: one to create it, one to validate it. This pair is the standard — do not add a contract without both.

Command Purpose Key flags Convention it enforces obs flow init [directory] Create .flow/obsidian-sync.yml --vault-root, --pairs (JSON), --force, --json Interactive and non-interactive mode; refuses overwrite without --force; atomic write + .bak backup obs doctor --layer flow [--vault X] Validate every vault's config --layer flow, --json 6 checks (below); warn/fail levels; part of default all_layers

docs.title: obs doctor --layer flow checks
docs.text:
Check ID Level Triggers when flow-sync-missing warn Vault has no .flow/obsidian-sync.yml flow-sync-schema fail File fails JSON Schema validation flow-sync-stale warn Config is > 90 days old flow-sync-vault-root warn vault_root path not found on disk flow-sync-pair-dup warn Duplicate vault→repo mapping flow-sync-pair-identity fail vault and repo are identical

Why two commands: creation is interactive-for-humans but scriptable-for-CI (--pairs JSON + --json); validation is what hooks into savant:restore, craft:recap, and MCP diagnose() so drift is caught at session start, not at sync time.

docs.title: 4. Obsidian Dashboards
docs.text:
A dashboard is a deterministic markdown view obs renders into a vault file. There are two, both following the same marker-bounded, atomic, zero-diff-on-unchanged standard.

Command Output file Source obs research board [--out F] [--kind K] _RESEARCH-BOARD.md atlas project list --json obs board refresh [--vault V] [--all] _ACTION-BOARD.md atlas + vault DB (ghost drift) + .STATUS

docs.title: Must
docs.text:
• Wrap all generated content in <!-- obs:board:start --> … <!-- obs:board:end --> markers; only the region between markers is replaced.
  • Write atomically via os.replace (marker-bounded region only).
  • Be deterministic: re-running on unchanged source state produces zero diff.
  • Support --dry-run: show what would change and exit non-zero when the file would change — this is the drift guard for cron/launchd.
  • Support --out <file> (write) vs. stdout (print) — stdout is the default.

docs.title: Must not
docs.text:
• Touch hand-written prose outside the markers.
  • Mutate the vault database or notes other than the single target file.
  • Embed non-deterministic content (timestamps in the body, sorted-by-time tables) that would break the zero-diff guarantee.

docs.title: Worked example
docs.text:
The marker block in the target file:

<!-- obs:board:start -->
| Manuscript | Venue | Status | Progress |
|------------|-------|--------|----------|
| Bridge calibration | JASA  | 🟢    | ████████░░ |
<!-- obs:board:end -->

Schedule a drift guard (exits non-zero if the board would change):

# crontab — nightly staleness check
obs research board --out ~/vault/00_meta/_RESEARCH-BOARD.md --dry-run \
  || echo "RESEARCH-BOARD drift detected"

docs.title: 5. Checklist for new surfaces
docs.text:
Copy this into a PR description. A new contract / command / dashboard is not done until every box is checked:

  • Contract validates against a JSON Schema in schema/ (not ad-hoc dict access).
  • Create command has both interactive and non-interactive (--json / --pairs) modes; refuses overwrite without --force; writes via os.replace; backs up on --force.
  • Validate command exists (obs doctor --layer flow style) with warn/fail levels and is wired into the default all_layers set.
  • Dashboard (if any) is marker-bounded, atomic, deterministic (zero diff on unchanged state), and supports --dry-run with non-zero exit on drift.
  • Path safety: no .. or leading / in any user-supplied path; no writes outside the intended tree.
  • Docs: this page updated; CLI Reference lists the command; Architecture → Config File Contracts lists the contract; mkdocs.yml nav includes any new page.
  • Tests: unit + (where it writes files) dogfood/e2e covering invalid input, overwrite refusal, and atomic write.
  • Verification: mkdocs build --strict and python3 -m pytest src/python/tests/test_doc_counts.py pass.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: TL;DR (30 seconds) - What: Install obs via Homebrew or manual setup - Why: Manage Obsidian vaults from the terminal in seconds - How: brew install data-wise/tap/obsidian-cli-ops - Next: Configuration for optional settings

docs.title: Homebrew (Recommended)
docs.text:
brew install data-wise/tap/obsidian-cli-ops

This installs obs with all Python dependencies in an isolated virtual environment (libexec/venv) and sets up the shell integration automatically. No manual pip step is ever needed, and a system Python upgrade won't break obs.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• macOS or Linux
  • Python 3.9+: python3 --version
  • ZSH: Default on macOS; available on Linux via apt install zsh
  • Git: For cloning the repository

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Clone the repository:

    git clone https://github.com/Data-Wise/obsidian-cli-ops.git ~/projects/obsidian-cli-ops
cd ~/projects/obsidian-cli-ops

  2. Run the installer (symlinks the CLI and provisions deps):

    ./install.sh

    This creates an isolated virtual environment at ~/.local/share/obs/venv, installs the pinned dependencies from requirements.lock, and symlinks the obs.zsh launcher into ~/.config/zsh/functions. It is idempotent — it only re-provisions when requirements.lock changes. No manual pip needed.

    Why not pip install?

    Installing into your system/ambient Python is fragile: a python@3.x minor upgrade silently drops the packages and obs breaks with ModuleNotFoundError. The isolated venv avoids this entirely.

  3. Enable shell autoload — add to your ~/.zshrc:

    fpath=(~/.config/zsh/functions $fpath)
autoload -Uz obs

  4. Initialize the database:

    python3 src/python/obs_cli.py db init

  5. Restart your shell:

    source ~/.zshrc

docs.title: How dependencies are provisioned
docs.text:
obs runs its bundled Python code against an interpreter that must have the core dependencies (rich, networkx, click, python-frontmatter, PyYAML, requests). Both install paths put those deps in a dedicated, isolated environment — never your system Python:

Install path Environment Source of pins Homebrew libexec/venv (formula-owned) formula resource blocks install.sh ~/.local/share/obs/venv requirements.lock

Each run, the launcher resolves OBS_PYTHON in priority order. It never silently trusts a bare python3 (that was the source of the historical ModuleNotFoundError: 'rich' crash):

flowchart TD
    Start([obs invoked]) --> Q1{"$OBS_PYTHON set<br/>and executable?"}
    Q1 -->|yes| U1[Use $OBS_PYTHON]
    Q1 -->|no| Q2{"no user venv<br/>and brew available?"}
    Q2 -->|yes| Q2b{"libexec/venv<br/>exists?"}
    Q2b -->|yes| U2[Use Homebrew libexec/venv]
    Q2b -->|no| Q3
    Q2 -->|no| Q3{"~/.local/share/obs/venv<br/>exists?"}
    Q3 -->|yes| U3[Use install.sh user venv]
    Q3 -->|no| Q4{"ambient python3<br/>on PATH?"}
    Q4 -->|yes| U4["Use ambient python3<br/>⚠️ warn: deps may be missing"]
    Q4 -->|no| Err["ERROR: no python3 found"]

You can always force a specific interpreter by exporting OBS_PYTHON (tier 1), which takes precedence over everything else.

docs.title: Verify Installation
docs.text:
# Check version
obs version

# List discovered vaults
obs

You should see the version number and any Obsidian vaults found in your iCloud directory.

docs.title: ModuleNotFoundError (e.g. No module named 'rich')
docs.text:
This means obs resolved to a Python without its deps — usually because no isolated environment exists yet. If you also see a [obs] WARN: ... ambient python3 ... dependencies may be missing line, that's the launcher telling you it fell through to tier 4. Provision an isolated env:

brew reinstall obsidian-cli-ops   # Homebrew
# or, for a manual checkout:
./install.sh

After a python@3.x upgrade via Homebrew, obs keeps working because its deps live in libexec/venv, not in the upgraded interpreter.

docs.title: Python not found
docs.text:
If obs reports a Python error, ensure /opt/homebrew/bin/python3 (macOS) or /usr/bin/python3 (Linux) exists. You can set a custom path:

export OBS_PYTHON=/path/to/python3

docs.title: ZSH autoload not working
docs.text:
Verify the function file is in your fpath:

echo $fpath | tr ' ' '\n' | grep obs

If nothing appears, double-check the symlink path and your ~/.zshrc configuration.

docs.title: Database initialization fails
docs.text:
Ensure the config directory exists:

mkdir -p ~/.config/obs
python3 src/python/obs_cli.py db init

docs.title: 2. R-Dev Integration
docs.text:
Why Removed: - R integration belongs in R package ecosystem - Added 307 lines to codebase - Limited to R users only - Better served by dedicated R package

Recommended Alternative:

Use R packages for Obsidian integration: - Create R package with usethis::create_package() - Use here::here() for path management - Use fs package for file operations - Consider creating dedicated R-Obsidian package

Example R Package Setup:

# In your R project
library(usethis)
library(fs)

# Create functions for Obsidian integration
write_to_obsidian <- function(content, vault_path) {
  path <- fs::path(vault_path, "R-Notes", paste0(Sys.Date(), ".md"))
  writeLines(content, path)
  message("✓ Written to Obsidian: ", path)
}

# Use it
write_to_obsidian("# Analysis Results\n\n...", "~/Vaults/Research")

Alternatives: - Plugin management: Use Obsidian's built-in Community Plugins interface - Vault auditing: Use obs stats <vault> - Configuration sync: Use git or cloud storage directly

docs.title: Graph Analysis
docs.text:
The analyze command calculates knowledge graph metrics:

obs analyze MyVault

Metrics include:

  • Density - How interconnected your vault is (0.0 to 1.0)
  • Clusters - Groups of tightly related notes
  • Hub notes - Highly connected central notes
  • Orphans - Notes with no links (may need integration)
  • Broken links - Wikilinks pointing to non-existent notes

Add -v for detailed output including top hub notes:

obs analyze MyVault -v

See the Cookbook for graph analysis recipes.

You only need Level 1 to get started.

docs.title: R-Dev Integration
docs.text: The r-dev module connects your R/Emacs workflow to your Obsidian "Lab Notebook".

docs.title: 1. Link a Project
docs.text:
Tell obs where this R project lives in your vault.

cd ~/projects/RMediation
obs r-dev link Research_Lab/RMediation_Package

This creates a mapping in ~/.config/obs/project_map.json so future commands auto-detect the correct Obsidian folder.

docs.title: 2. Check Status (Optional)
docs.text:
See if the current R project is linked.

obs r-dev status

Shows: - R project root path - Mapped Obsidian folder - Whether the mapping exists

docs.title: 3. Log Results
docs.text:
Push simulation plots or HTML reports to the 06_Analysis folder.

obs r-dev log results/plot.png -m "Sensitivity analysis n=500"

Files are automatically timestamped to prevent overwrites.

docs.title: 4. Fetch Theory
docs.text:
Grab mathematical context from your Knowledge Base while coding.

obs r-dev context "Sobel Test"

docs.title: 5. Sync Drafts
docs.text:
Push a vignette or RMarkdown file to 02_Drafts for prose editing in Obsidian.

obs r-dev draft vignettes/intro.Rmd

docs.title: 6. Unlink a Project
docs.text:
Remove the R project mapping when you're done.

cd ~/projects/RMediation
obs r-dev unlink

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Use obs list to see all your R project mappings at a glance
  • Use --verbose flag to debug mapping issues: obs --verbose r-dev log plot.png
  • The mapping file is plain JSON, you can edit ~/.config/obs/project_map.json directly if needed

docs.title: v2.0 Knowledge Graph Features
docs.text: The v2.0 release transforms obs into an intelligent knowledge management system with powerful graph analysis capabilities.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
v2.0 adds a Python-powered backend that:

  • Scans your Obsidian vaults and extracts all metadata
  • Analyzes the knowledge graph structure
  • Calculates importance metrics for every note
  • Detects orphans, hubs, and broken links
  • Tracks vault statistics over time

All data is stored locally in a SQLite database at ~/.config/obs/vault_db.sqlite.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
# Install Python dependencies

docs.title: Basic Workflow
docs.text:
# 1. Discover vaults in a directory
obs discover ~/Documents -v

# 2. Scan and analyze a vault

# 3. View results

docs.title: Markdown Parsing
docs.text:
Extracts comprehensive metadata from every note:

  • Frontmatter: YAML metadata
  • Title: From frontmatter, first H1, or filename
  • Wikilinks: [[target]] and [[target|display]]
  • Tags: Both #tag and #nested/tag
  • Timestamps: Created and modified dates
  • Statistics: Word count, character count

docs.title: Link Resolution
docs.text:
Intelligently resolves wikilinks to actual notes:

  1. Exact path match
  2. Path without .md extension
  3. Relative path from source note
  4. Filename-only match

Broken links are detected and tracked in the database.

docs.title: PageRank
docs.text: Importance score based on link structure (like Google's algorithm). Notes that are linked to by important notes get higher scores.

docs.title: Degree Centrality
docs.text:
• In-degree: How many notes link to this one
  • Out-degree: How many notes this one links to

docs.title: Betweenness Centrality
docs.text: How often a note appears on the shortest path between other notes. High betweenness = bridge between topics.

docs.title: Closeness Centrality
docs.text: Average distance to all other notes in the graph. High closeness = well-connected.

docs.title: Clustering Coefficient
docs.text: How connected a note's neighbors are to each other. High clustering = tightly-knit topic cluster.

docs.title: Orphaned Notes
docs.text:
Notes with no incoming or outgoing links. These might need better integration into your knowledge graph.

obs stats <vault>

Look for "Orphaned notes" count.

docs.title: Hub Notes
docs.text:
Notes with more than 10 total connections (in + out). These are central to your knowledge base.

obs analyze <vault> -v

Shows top 5 hub notes with connection counts.

docs.title: Broken Links
docs.text:
Wikilinks that don't resolve to any note. Might be typos or deleted notes.

obs stats <vault>

Shows broken link count and sources.

docs.title: Database Schema
docs.text: The SQLite database contains:

docs.title: Tables
docs.text:
• vaults: Vault metadata
  • notes: All notes with content hashes
  • links: Wikilink relationships
  • tags: Tag definitions
  • note_tags: Many-to-many tag associations
  • graph_metrics: Calculated metrics
  • scan_history: Scan tracking

docs.title: Views
docs.text:
• orphaned_notes: Notes with no links
  • hub_notes: Highly connected notes (>10 links)
  • broken_links: Unresolved wikilinks

docs.title: Auto-Updates
docs.text: Triggers automatically update: - Vault note counts - Tag usage counts - Graph in/out degrees

docs.title: 1. Vault Health Check
docs.text:
# Scan vault
obs discover ~/Documents/Obsidian/MyVault --scan -v

# Get vault ID
obs vaults

# Check stats
obs stats <vault>

Look for: - High orphan count → Need more linking - Many broken links → Clean up or update links - Low density → Isolated clusters

docs.title: 2. Find Important Notes
docs.text:
# Analyze graph
obs analyze <vault> -v

Top hub notes are your most connected concepts. Consider: - Adding more detail to these notes - Breaking them into sub-topics if too large - Ensuring they're well-maintained

docs.title: 3. Discover Gaps
docs.text: Notes with high betweenness but low in-degree are bridges between topics but not well-documented themselves. Great candidates for expansion.

docs.title: 4. Track Over Time
docs.text:
Re-scan regularly and compare: 

# Scan weekly
obs discover ~/Documents --scan -v

# Track stats
obs stats <vault>

Watch for: - Growing orphan count - Increasing broken links - Changing hub notes

docs.title: Scanning Speed
docs.text:
• ~100 notes/second on modern hardware
  • 1,000 note vault: ~10 seconds
  • 10,000 note vault: ~2 minutes

docs.title: Analysis Speed
docs.text:
• Link resolution: O(n) with caching
  • PageRank: O(n × iterations)
  • Centrality: O(n²) for betweenness/closeness

Large vaults (>10k notes) may take a few minutes for full analysis.

docs.title: Memory Usage
docs.text:
• Database: ~1KB per note
  • NetworkX graph: ~100 bytes per edge
  • 10,000 note vault with 50,000 links: ~100MB RAM

from vault_scanner import VaultScanner

from db_manager import DatabaseManager

docs.title: Release Notes v3.0.0
docs.text: Release Date: 2026-03-05 Previous Release: v2.2.0 (2025-12-20)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
v3.0.0 is a major release that transforms Obsidian CLI Ops into a laser-focused vault management tool with AI-powered graph analysis. The codebase was simplified from 11,500 to ~7,400 lines (36% reduction) while adding powerful new capabilities.

Philosophy: "Do one thing exceptionally well — manage Obsidian vaults."

docs.title: Simplified CLI (Phase 7.1)
docs.text:
• 20+ commands → 15 focused commands — eliminated feature overlap with other tools
  • ZSH-First Architecture — fast shell integration with Python core
  • Removed TUI (1,701 lines) — CLI-only for simplicity and maintainability
  • Removed R-Dev integration (307 lines) — belongs in R package ecosystem
  • Removed legacy v1.x commands (126 lines) — plugin install, sync, audit

docs.title: Multi-Provider AI System (Phase 7.2)
docs.text:
• 5 AI providers: Gemini API, Anthropic API, Ollama, Gemini CLI, Claude CLI
  • Smart routing: auto-selects best provider for each operation type
  • Modern SDKs: migrated to google-genai (replacing deprecated google-generativeai), added anthropic SDK
  • Shared models: AnalysisResult, ComparisonResult, SimilarNote dataclasses with from_json() validation
  • Embedding cache: SQLite-backed note_embeddings table with mtime invalidation
  • Retry with backoff: exponential backoff decorator on all API methods
  • Obsidian CLI bridge: integrates with Obsidian's native CLI for backlinks and orphan data

docs.title: New AI Commands
docs.text: Command Description obs ai suggest-links <note> Find unlinked related notes using embeddings obs ai gaps <vault> Detect stub notes, orphans, and knowledge gaps obs ai summarize <vault> Generate theme analysis across entire vault obs ai refactor <vault> AI-powered vault reorganization suggestions

docs.title: Vault Health Dashboard (Phase 7.3)
docs.text:
• obs health <vault> — comprehensive health scores with 4 dimensions:
  • Connectivity (orphan ratio)
  • Link Integrity (broken link count)
  • Structure (tag coverage, hub balance)
  • Freshness (stale note detection)
  • Rich progress bar visualization in terminal
  • --json flag on all 10 data-outputting commands for scripting

docs.title: Vault Name/Prefix Lookup
docs.text:
• Use vault names directly: obs analyze Knowledge_Base instead of hex IDs
  • Prefix matching: obs analyze e947 resolves to the matching vault
  • Ambiguous prefix feedback: clear error when multiple vaults match

docs.title: CLI Polish
docs.text:
• --verbose flag wired to all AI commands (suggest-links, gaps, summarize)
  • Better error messages with tips: "Run 'obs discover ' to find new vaults"
  • Version consistency enforced across 5 files via automated tests

docs.title: Removed Commands
docs.text: Removed Replacement obs switch <vault> Use obs analyze <vault> directly obs open, obs sync Use Obsidian app directly obs tui Removed — CLI-only interface obs r-dev * Use R package tools directly obs install, obs audit Removed — v1.x legacy

  • google-generativeai replaced by google-genai (Gemini SDK migration)
  • anthropic added as optional dependency

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
All public API methods raise typed exceptions from src/python/core/exceptions.py:

Exception When Raised VaultNotFoundError vault_id not registered in database NoteNotFoundError note_id not found in database VaultScanError Filesystem errors during scanning AIProviderError All AI providers unavailable DatabaseError SQLite operation failure

MCP tools catch all exceptions and return structured error JSON rather than propagating to the stdio transport.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Version: 4.3.0

Obsidian CLI Ops follows a clean four-layer architecture: Presentation, Application (Core), AI Features, and Data — plus an MCP Integration layer added in v3.3.0.

    subgraph Presentation["Presentation Layer"]

        P[obs_cli.py\n985 lines]
    end

    subgraph MCP["MCP Integration Layer (v3.3.0)"]
        M[mcp_server.py\n42 tools · 4 resources]
    end

    subgraph Core["Application Layer (Core)"]
        VM[VaultManager]
        GA[GraphAnalyzer]
        DM[Domain Models]
    end

    subgraph AI["AI Features Layer (Optional)"]
        AR[AIRouter]

    end

    subgraph Data["Data Layer"]
        DB[DatabaseManager]
        VS[VaultScanner]
        GB[GraphBuilder]
        SQ[(SQLite\nvault_db)]

    end

    Z --> P
    P --> VM
    P --> GA
    M --> P
    VM --> DB
    GA --> DB
    VM --> VS
    VS --> FS
    FT --> DB
    FV --> DB
    FR --> DB
    AR --> PR
    DB --> SQ
    GB --> SQ

Key principle: Business logic lives in the Core layer only. Both the ZSH CLI and the MCP server are thin presentation layers that call obs_cli.py subprocesses or Python APIs.

  • obs_cli.py — Python CLI. Argparse subcommands, calls Core/AI methods, formats output with Rich.

docs.title: Design Patterns
docs.text: Pattern Where Used Repository DatabaseManager wraps all SQLite operations Facade VaultManager / GraphAnalyzer simplify complex multi-step operations Factory from_db_row() class methods on every domain model Dependency Injection Core classes accept an optional DatabaseManager Null Object ObsidianBridge returns empty results when Obsidian CLI unavailable Strategy AIRouter selects among 5 interchangeable provider strategies Adapter Each AI provider adapts a different API to the common AIProvider interface AST-walk note_inserter uses markdown-it-py token stream to locate headings — immune to headings inside fenced code blocks

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Script: src/python/generate_test_vault.py

Purpose: Creates realistic synthetic Obsidian vaults with configurable: - Number of notes (1-1000+) - Link density (0.0-1.0) - Tag distribution - Content variety

Special Features: - Generates .obsidian directory (valid Obsidian vault) - Creates wikilinks with proper [[link]] and [[link|alias]] syntax - Adds YAML frontmatter (30% of notes) - Includes special test notes (orphan, hub, broken links, index) - Reproducible with --seed parameter

docs.title: Usage
docs.text: python3 src/python/generate_test_vault.py <output_dir> [options]

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Option Short Default Description --notes -n 20 Number of notes to generate --density -d 0.3 Link density (avg links/note as fraction) --tags -t 10 Number of unique tags --seed -s None Random seed for reproducibility

  --notes 10 --density 0.2 --tags 5

  --notes 50 --density 0.3 --tags 15

# Large vault (stress test)

  --notes 200 --density 0.4 --tags 30

# Reproducible vault (same content every time)

  --notes 20 --seed 42

docs.title: Batch Vault Generation
docs.text:
Generate multiple test vaults at once:

#!/bin/bash
# batch_generate.sh

for size in small medium large; do
  case $size in
    small)  notes=10; density=0.2; tags=5 ;;
    medium) notes=50; density=0.3; tags=15 ;;
    large)  notes=200; density=0.4; tags=30 ;;
  esac

  python3 src/python/generate_test_vault.py \
    ~/Documents/TestVault-$size \
    --notes $notes --density $density --tags $tags

  python3 src/python/obs_cli.py discover ~/Documents/TestVault-$size --scan
done

echo "✅ All test vaults generated and scanned!"

  • scan_history: Scan tracking and analytics
  • DatabaseManager: Complete CRUD API for all operations
  • Vault management (add, get, list, update)
  • Note operations (add, get, list, exists)
  • Link queries (outgoing, incoming, broken)
  • Tag operations (add, get stats)

docs.title: 2. Vault Scanner (src/python/vault_scanner.py)
docs.text:
• VaultScanner: Orchestrates vault discovery and scanning
  • discover_vaults(): Finds vaults by .obsidian directory
  • scan_vault(): Parses all markdown files and populates database
  • MarkdownParser: Extracts all metadata from notes
  • Frontmatter parsing (YAML)
  • Wikilink extraction: [[target|display]]
  • Tag extraction: #tag, #nested/tag
  • Title extraction (frontmatter → H1 → filename)
  • Word count and file metadata

docs.title: 3. Graph Builder (src/python/graph_builder.py)
docs.text:
• LinkResolver: Resolves wikilinks to actual note IDs
  • Handles multiple link formats
  • Relative path resolution
  • Marks broken links
  • GraphBuilder: NetworkX-based graph analysis
  • build_graph(): Constructs directed graph from database
  • calculate_metrics(): Computes all graph metrics
    • PageRank (importance score)
    • In/out degree (connection counts)
    • Betweenness centrality
    • Closeness centrality
    • Clustering coefficient
  • find_clusters(): Community detection
  • get_note_neighborhood(): Subgraph extraction

docs.title: 4. CLI Integration (src/python/obs_cli.py + src/obs.zsh)
docs.text:
• Python CLI: Full-featured command-line interface
  • discover: Find and scan vaults
  • scan: Scan individual vault
  • analyze: Run graph analysis
  • vaults: List all vaults
  • stats: Show statistics
  • db init: Initialize database
  • ZSH Integration: Seamless integration with obs command
  • obs discover [path]: Discover vaults
  • obs analyze <vault>: Analyze graph

docs.title: Why HuggingFace as Default?
docs.text: Reasoning: 1. Pure Python - no external services 2. Works everywhere (Mac, Linux, Windows) 3. Free forever (no quotas) 4. Easy installation (pip install) 5. Good performance for light usage

docs.title: Why Ollama as Alternative?
docs.text: Reasoning: 1. Fast processing for power users 2. Reasoning capabilities (chat models) 3. Flexible model choices 4. Active development 5. Can use very small models (qwen2.5:0.5b = 500MB)

Solution: - Implemented free alternatives only - Made paid APIs optional in requirements.txt (commented out) - Multi-provider architecture allows future additions
